issues: Dolphin is rendered as a flat, hard-edged filled polygon with horizontal scanline striping — reads as a CAD/fish silhouette, not a lit phosphor creature; lacks smooth organic curvature, rim light, and a clear pectoral fin; tail fluke is stubby.

Dolphin is too small and parked in the upper third instead of arcing across the central 50-60% of display height, so it does not dominate; the wide bright FFT band and wave stack at the bottom pull the eye away.
No phosphor bloom/halo around any element — everything sits as crisp flat cyan on pure black, missing the soft OEL glow that defines the reference look.
No persistence/afterglow trail behind the dolphin; the characteristic short phosphor persistence of a moving OEL object is entirely absent.
FFT bar graph is too tall (closer to 20-25% of height) and too high-contrast, competing with the dolphin rather than receding to ~13% low-contrast.
Water-surface lines form a bright multi-row band that is more prominent than the 'subtle, subordinate 2-3 rows' the reference calls for.
Horizontal line texture inside the dolphin body looks like a fill artifact rather than phosphor emission, flattening the form.
suggestions: Redraw the dolphin much larger so its arc fills the central 50-60% of the 320x128 frame, with smooth bezier body curvature, a defined dorsal fin, a swept tail fluke, a visible pectoral fin, and a brighter 1px rim-light edge to give it volume.
Add a subtle phosphor bloom: a tight bright core with a soft 2-4px falloff halo so the dolphin reads as an emitting OEL object, not a flat vector — keep it crisp, not blown out.
Introduce a short, clean persistence trail (2-3 fading ghost frames) behind the dolphin's motion path to evoke OEL afterglow without fogging the whole scene.
Replace the flat scanline fill inside the dolphin with an edge-bright / interior-dim phosphor gradient so the body looks lit rather than textured.
Shrink the FFT band to ~13% of height and drop its brightness/contrast so it sits as a quiet footer beneath the dolphin.
Reduce the water lines to 2 thin, low-contrast rows occupying <=15% height, clearly subordinate to the dolphin.
Re-balance overall luminance so the eye travels dolphin -> top track text -> waves -> FFT, with the dolphin unmistakably the brightest, largest mass.
